records.text_tokens: a small sql experiment with filtered nearest neighbours text matches and reciprocal rank fusion including the results that disappear when limit comes too early suppose i have a table of specimen notes and want to find something about a failed library preparation some notes use exactly those words while others describe the same problem as “too little material after amplification” i would like both to appear but only if they belong to the study i am currently looking at there are two separate decisions here which rows are allowed into the answer and how to order those rows keeping them separate makes it much easier to explain why a search returned something odd especially when more than one search method contributes results the term hybrid search is used for both combining lexical and semantic retrieval and combining vector retrieval with ordinary filters i want to look at the boundary between these two uses with a deliberately small sql experiment the numbers below are invented distances and ranks so the examples require postgresql but no embedding model or additional extension losing a row before the search is finished here are four notes already assigned distances from a query smaller means closer only study a is relevant to the request and i want two results with notes id study distance as values 11 b 0 04 12 a 0 08 13 b 0 10 14 a 0 16 nearest as select from notes order by distance id limit 2 filtered first as select from notes where study a order by distance id limit 2 select limit then filter as approach array agg id order by distance id as ids from nearest where study a union all select filter then limit array agg id order by distance id from filtered first the first answer contains only note 12 note 14 never gets a chance because the inner query has already discarded it increasing the final limit cannot bring it back this is a consequence of where i put the limit even with perfectly accurate distances and no index involved the id is a tie breaker which makes the example reproducible if two distances become equal postgresql does not promise which tied rows a limited query will choose unless the ordering distinguishes them that matters for tests and for a reader trying the example twice postgresql s limit documentation describes this behaviour where an approximate index changes the problem with pgvector an approximate index can find nearby candidates without comparing the query against every stored embedding filters are applied to those candidates which means a restrictive study filter can leave fewer results than requested iterative scans available since pgvector 0 8 0 can continue looking but scan limits still matter an ordered result also does not prove that every closer eligible row was found pgvector documents both filtering and iterative scans for a small eligible subset i would first measure an exact distance sort after filtering then compare an approximate plan against that answer there is no universal row count at which one becomes better the distance calculation the distribution of studies and the amount of data all enter the measurement having an index on the study column and another on embeddings does not by itself settle that choice postgresql can combine suitable index scans through bitmaps but the bitmap represents matching table locations and loses the original index ordering an ordered nearest neighbour search needs more than a set of matching locations combining multiple indexes explains the bitmap part combining two ranked lists now suppose the eligible notes have been searched twice a lexical search found note 21 first while the embedding search preferred note 24 postgresql s built in text search can produce the lexical matches and a relevance ranking its scores describe that ranking method not a probability that a note answers the question the text search documentation explains the available ranking functions i do not want to add a text score directly to a vector distance their scales and directions have different meanings for this experiment i use reciprocal rank fusion instead adding 1 60 position for each list containing a note a missing note contributes nothing the constant 60 comes from the original rrf paper it is a choice to evaluate not a property of postgresql cormack clarke and buettcher 2009 with lexical note id position as values 21 1 24 2 28 3 semantic note id position as values 24 1 31 2 21 3 contributions as select note id 1 0 60 position as weight from lexical union all select note id 1 0 60 position from semantic select note id round sum weight 6 as fused score from contributions group by note id order by sum weight desc note id note 24 wins because it appears near the top of both lists note 31 still appears even though the lexical search did not find it union all is intentional each list provides its own contribution within each input list however a note must occur only once otherwise joins that duplicate rows would accidentally give it extra votes this is a useful place to stop and inspect the candidates fusion cannot recover a note absent from both lists and asking each method for only two candidates may remove a note that would have done well in the combined ranking i would choose candidate limits separately from the number of results displayed to the reader what i would measure for each test query i would keep the eligible ids each candidate list and the final ordering together with the query time this makes a missing result traceable was it excluded by the study filter absent from retrieval or just ranked too low a single response time number cannot answer that i would also include awkward cases a rare study a note containing an exact sample identifier two notes with tied scores and a query with no lexical match the occasional empty answer is less suprising when those cases are part of the test data from the beginning the tiny datasets here are a way to inspect the decisions in sql before choosing an index or a larger retrieval setup

laboratory notes in postgresql a copy of the database directory ends up on a misplaced disk while the database itself is still running somewhere else i want the copied files to be unreadable but i also want the application to carry on using ordinary select statements without adding a decryption call to every query that is the useful part of transparent data encryption or tde the word feature says it supports vectors i still need to ask what i can put into it and which operations it supports a vector might be a value stored in one row a collection of values being processed together or the outline of an illustration on this page those uses can appear in the same application without sharing an implementation i find it easier to start with a sample record than with the word itself imagine a specimen with a free text note three measurements and a position on a laboratory diagram all three belong to the sample but searching the note comparing measurements and drawing its position are separate tasks the vector made of words postgresql s tsvector stores lexemes which are the normalized terms used by full text search with optional positions and weights it is not a list of embedding coordinates i can inspect the difference using a note that mentions the same thing twice with note as select to tsvector english samples were frozen the second sample thawed as terms select terms terms plainto tsquery english frozen sample as matches from note the rendered value is organized by lexeme so it no longer looks like the original sentence positions preserve information about where terms occurred a tsquery supplies the search condition and tests whether the document representation matches it there is no embedding model hidden inside this query text search types and text search operators describe the two types and their relationship for these examples i name the english configuration explicitly a sample identifier is a different problem from ordinary english prose and i would inspect its tokenization before deciding to feed it through the same configuration in particular turning a note into searchable terms is not a reversible way to store the note itself i would keep the original text as well a list of numbers still needs a meaning three measurements fit in a postgresql array although their interpretation remains part of the schema and the application here i have arranged them in the order concentration volume and temperature the database cannot infer those labels from the array with sample measurements as values array 12 5 40 0 4 0 real select measurements 1 as concentration measurements 2 as volume measurements 3 as temperature cardinality measurements as dimensions from sample writing an array declaration with a size such as real 3 does not enforce that size in postgresql if i need exactly three entries i must enforce that separately and array bounds deserve attention too if values can arrive from outside the application the array documentation covers these details even when two arrays have the same length blindly computing their distance might be meaningless a change of one degree and a change of one microlitre are different quantities converting just one measurement to another unit would change the numerical distance that is a modelling decision not something an index can fix an embedding also contains numbers but its coordinates come from a chosen representation of the input pgvector supplies a vector type and distance operators for this use the following optional example requires the separately installed pgvector extension it uses invented coordinates rather than real specimen embeddings create extension if not exists vector select 0 2 0 4 0 6 vector 3 0 2 0 4 0 9 vector 3 as distance here means euclidean distance for those operand types choosing a distance and generating comparable inputs remain separate from storing the values the pgvector reference lists the supported operators in an actual experiment i would record the embedding model and preprocessing alongside the data so a later model change cannot quietly mix incompatible representations the same operator can describe a different distance a point on a two dimensional laboratory drawing does not need an embedding extension postgresql already has geometric types including point and the point to point distance operator is also written select point 2 3 as storage position point 5 7 as workbench position point 2 3 point 5 7 as drawing distance this returns a distance of five drawing units the type tells postgresql which operation to perform even though the operator spelling is shared with the previous example these built in coordinates describe a plane they do not carry a geographic coordinate reference system geometric types and their operators specify the available operations vector graphics add another use of the word the illustration above consists of shapes and text while an svg path can describe a shape through drawing commands and coordinates the browser paints that description at the requested size those coordinates are instructions for an image not a search representation of its meaning the svg path specification explains that format a vector can also span many rows vectorized execution refers to how a database processes data internally for example duckdb s execution format passes batches of values through operators and a batch can contain ordinary integers or strings its documentation distinguishes several physical representations including flat and constant vectors the sql column does not have to contain embeddings for this execution method to be useful duckdb describes these representations in its execution format documentation that distinction prevents an occassional misunderstanding adding a vector column to a postgresql table does not by itself turn the query executor into a batch processing engine a stored value s type and the way an executor moves through rows answer different questions when reading about a vector feature i therefore try to identify the stored value the operation and the execution method separately for the specimen example those questions lead to fairly ordinary choices retain the note define the measurements name the coordinate system and test the search behaviour the shared vocabulary becomes much less troublesome once those choices are written down

records.title: Why are alignment fields NULL in a plain SELECT?
records.summary: Alignment fields describe a match produced by a search. Reading a row on its own does not create an alignment context, so a field such as bioseq.score has no match to describe. Select it in the alignment query shown in the walkthrough. Some details also depend on which alignment work the query requests and which settings are enabled.

records.title: Does the 120× speedup apply to every query?
records.summary: No. “Up to 120×” refers to particular measured comparisons, not every workload. Reusing a prepared index, available memory, sequence sizes, and the comparison tool's work all affect the result. Building the index also costs time.
